target_constraint: Must maintain screw preload under masticatory forces for 15+ years
observed_phenomenon: Implant-abutment screw loosening causing restoration failure
mechanism: Piezoelectric materials convert mechanical energy (e.g., masticatory loading) into local electrical signals, which can be used to actively counteract mechanical loosening by generating controlled micro-displacements or surface-level forces that maintain contact pressure at the implant-abutment interface.
intervention: Integrate a piezoelectric ceramic layer (e.g., a thin film or washer) at the implant-abutment screw interface. Under occlusal loading, the piezoelectric element generates a local electrical potential that drives a small, controlled counter-torque or compressive strain on the screw threads, actively compensating for preload loss and preventing screw loosening over 15+ years.
expected_effect: The piezoelectric element converts cyclic masticatory forces into a self-regulating mechanical counter-force that maintains screw preload, reducing the incidence of abutment screw loosening and subsequent restoration failure.
falsification_test: In a cyclic loading fatigue test (e.g., 10^6 cycles at 200 N, 5 Hz) on implant-abutment assemblies with and without the piezoelectric layer, measure screw removal torque. If the piezoelectric group does not show significantly higher retained torque (e.g., >80% of initial preload) compared to the torque-controlled baseline, the mechanism is falsified.
source_spans: piezoelectric materials can convert mechanical energy into local electrical signals under occlusal loading, cell traction, or ultrasonic stimulation
